import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Read the data
data = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

# Create a figure with multiple subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))

# Define a color palette for brands
brand_colors = sns.color_palette("husl", n_colors=len(data['brand'].unique()))
brand_color_map = dict(zip(data['brand'].unique(), brand_colors))

# 1. Price vs Megapixels scatter plot
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 1)
for brand in data['brand'].unique():
    brand_data = data[data['brand'] == brand]
    plt.scatter(brand_data['megapixels'], brand_data['price_usd'], 
               label=brand, s=100, alpha=0.7, color=brand_color_map[brand])
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=10)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
plt.title('Price vs Megapixels by Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
plt.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 2. Weight vs Price scatter plot
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 2)
for brand in data['brand'].unique():
    brand_data = data[data['brand'] == brand]
    plt.scatter(brand_data['weight_grams'], brand_data['price_usd'], 
               label=brand, s=100, alpha=0.7, color=brand_color_map[brand])
plt.xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=10)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
plt.title('Price vs Weight by Brand', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
plt.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)

# 3. Sensor Type distribution
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 3)
sensor_counts = data['sensor_type'].value_counts()
colors = sns.color_palette("Set2", n_colors=len(sensor_counts))
plt.pie(sensor_counts.values, labels=sensor_counts.index, autopct='%1.1f%%',
        colors=colors, startangle=90)
plt.title('Sensor Type Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 4. Body Type distribution
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 4)
body_counts = data['body_type'].value_counts()
colors = sns.color_palette("Set3", n_colors=len(body_counts))
plt.bar(body_counts.index, body_counts.values, color=colors, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
plt.xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=10)
plt.ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
plt.title('Body Type Distribution', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# 5. 4K Video capability
ax5 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 5)
video_4k = data['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
labels = ['No 4K', '4K']
colors = ['#ff9999', '#66b3ff']
plt.pie(video_4k.values, labels=[labels[i] for i in video_4k.index], 
        autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors, startangle=90)
plt.title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')

# 6. Price by Brand
ax6 = plt.subplot(2, 3, 6)
brands = data['brand'].values
prices = data['price_usd'].values
colors_bar = [brand_color_map[brand] for brand in brands]
bars = plt.bar(range(len(brands)), prices, color=colors_bar, alpha=0.7, edgecolor='black')
plt.xlabel('Camera Index', fontsize=10)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=10)
plt.title('Price Comparison Across Cameras', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
plt.xticks(range(len(brands)), [f"{brand}\n{year}" for brand, year in zip(data['brand'], data['model_year'])], 
           fontsize=8, rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
